search_surface: Targeted PyPI project pages and project documentation for the first nine leads; then the PyPI Simple JSON project-name index filtered locally (six name queries, first 100 alphabetical hits each) with a top-15,000 PyPI package list used only to pick plausible high-adoption leads; see registry-snapshot.json

adoption_metric.name: PyPI Stats last_month downloads excluding known mirrors
adoption_metric.observation_window: rolling last month at capture time
adoption_metric.limitation: Package downloads are an ecosystem adoption proxy, not JSON-specific use; dependent installs inflate some counts. These values do not rank unverified leads.

leads.name: pydantic-core
leads.reason: pydantic_core.from_json is documented, but pydantic 2.14.3 requires pydantic-core==2.50.4, the same compiled extension and embedded Jiter 0.18.0 already measured by the selected pydantic path. Counting it would duplicate that binary and parser; not run.

leads.name: pandas
leads.reason: pandas.read_json returns a DataFrame or Series, not the parsed JSON value tree, so it cannot reproduce the exact type-tagged oracle tree of the nested controls. Its decoder is a vendored UltraJSON-derived copy (UltraJSON family, like the selected ujson path). Documentation-only check; not run.

leads.name: pyarrow
leads.reason: pyarrow.json.read_json reads line-delimited JSON objects into an Arrow Table with inferred column types; a top-level array such as the nested-array control is not a supported row, and the result is not a JSON value tree. Documentation-only check; not run.

leads.name: jiter
leads.family_hint: Jiter (same Rust parser family as pydantic-core; not independent)

leads.name: polars
leads.reason: polars.read_json returns a DataFrame with an inferred schema, not the parsed JSON value tree. Documentation-only check; not run.

leads.name: json5
leads.api_hint: json5.loads(local bytes or str); json5.load(local binary stream)
leads.family_hint: json5 pure-Python glop-generated PEG parser (JSON5 superset; own parser, no stdlib json delegation)

leads.name: json-repair
leads.reason: On valid input the documented default (json_repair.loads/load/from_file with skip_json_loads=False) returns the standard json.loads result (json_repair.py line 178); a host probe (python3 -I, pinned 0.64.9 wheel) saw json.loads, JSONDecoder.decode and raw_decode called on both valid controls, so this path is the CPython json family. The package's own repair parser runs only with skip_json_loads=True, which the pinned README documents as only for inputs already known to be invalid ("valid inputs should use the default behavior") and warns may change valid JSON. That parser was not selected: its documented use is malformed input, outside this valid-control gate. The same probe found its output equal to the oracle tree on both controls with no json call, but no container, coverage or AFL++ feedback was built.

leads.name: srsly
leads.reason: srsly 3.0.1 no longer vendors a ujson fork: srsly/_json_api.py json_loads/read_json call ujson.loads/ujson.load from its ujson>=5.11.0,<6 dependency. A re-export of the selected UltraJSON family (at an older ujson release), not a separate path.

leads.name: partial-json-parser
leads.reason: partial_json_parser/core/api.py completes truncated text and then calls the standard json.loads by default; shares the CPython json family.

leads.name: dirtyjson
leads.api_hint: dirtyjson.loads(local bytes or str); dirtyjson.load(local binary stream)
leads.family_hint: dirtyjson pure-Python lenient decoder (dirtyjson/loader.py), a rewritten simplejson loader (simplejson-derived lineage)

leads.name: hjson
leads.api_hint: hjson.loads(local bytes or str); hjson.load(local binary stream)
leads.family_hint: hjson-py pure-Python Hjson decoder (hjson/decoder.py), based on simplejson (simplejson-derived lineage)

leads.name: python-rapidjson
leads.family_hint: RapidJSON C++ (Tencent; same family as the C++ RapidJSON path)
leads.reason: Passed every gate (both valid controls, container control, parser-source coverage, stable AFL++ feedback) as a selected path until hjson (4,411,122) was verified with more downloads; it now ranks below the ten-path ceiling (tenth: hjson 4,411,122). Catalog row, verification record and receipts are kept in ceiling-displaced.json.

leads.name: pyjson5
leads.reason: Own Cython/C++ JSON5 decoder (src/_decoder.pyx), unrelated to the json5 package. Not run: its downloads are below the tenth selected path (hjson 4,411,122), so it could not enter the ten-path ceiling even if verified.

leads.name: commentjson
leads.reason: commentjson.loads strips comments with a lark grammar and then calls the standard json.loads (commentjson.py line 185); shares the CPython json family.

leads.name: json-stream-rs-tokenizer
leads.reason: Rust tokenizer backend for json-stream rather than a value-tree API of its own; would be evaluated through the json-stream path. Not run: its downloads are below the tenth selected path (hjson 4,411,122), so it could not enter the ten-path ceiling even if verified.

leads.name: json-stream
leads.reason: Own streaming JSON reader with a pure-Python tokenizer; by default select_tokenizer.py uses the Rust tokenizer from the json-stream-rs-tokenizer dependency. Not run: its downloads are below the tenth selected path (hjson 4,411,122), so it could not enter the ten-path ceiling even if verified.

leads.name: jsonnet
leads.reason: The Python binding evaluates the Jsonnet configuration language and returns JSON text, not a parsed JSON value tree. Not run.

leads.name: pysimdjson
leads.family_hint: simdjson 5.1.1 C++ (same family as C++ simdjson 5.0.4 pilot)
leads.reason: Passed every gate (both valid controls, container control, parser-source coverage, stable AFL++ feedback) as a selected path until dirtyjson (5,671,026) was verified with more downloads; it now ranks below the ten-path ceiling (tenth: hjson 4,411,122). Catalog row, verification record and receipts are kept in ceiling-displaced.json.

leads.name: demjson3
leads.reason: Own pure-Python JSON parser in demjson3.py; downloads are below every selected path. Not run.

leads.name: jsonslicer
leads.reason: Streaming C extension that, per its PyPI README, uses the YAJL library (same family as the ijson yajl2_c backend); not checked from source. Not run.

leads.name: json-five
leads.reason: Own pure-Python JSON5 parser; downloads are below every selected path. Not run.

leads.name: yapic-json
leads.reason: Own C++ JSON extension; downloads are far below every selected path. Not run.

leads.name: cysimdjson
leads.reason: Cython binding over simdjson (same family as the selected pysimdjson path). Not run.

leads.name: yyjson
leads.reason: CPython binding over the yyjson C library (orjson vendors the same C syntax parser). Not run.

leads.name: hyperjson
leads.reason: Per its PyPI README a thin wrapper around Rust serde_json via PyO3; a handful of monthly downloads. Not run.
